references.text: Jesus' speech about the judgment on the ruler of this world echoes directly in John 16:11, where he explains that the Holy Spirit will convince the world concerning judgment, precisely because the ruler of this world has been judged.
In John 14:30, Jesus confirms that the ruler of this world is coming, but has no power over him, which underscores the decisive victory and expulsion proclaimed.
The contrast between the world's suffering and Jesus' victory in John 16:33 builds on the fundamental victory over the ruler of this world that is declared.
Revelation describes the final execution of judgment upon 'the ancient serpent' and the ruler of this world, which is the same motif of expulsion that Jesus proclaims.
Peter warns that the devil, who is the ruler of this world, goes around like a roaring lion, which requires awareness of his defeat and limited power.

Paul refers to 'the prince of the power of the air' who works in the children of disobedience, a title that corresponds with 'the ruler of this world' and underscores the cosmic dimension of judgment.
